analysis: The code snippet calls `System.getProperty` multiple times to set default preferences. The `getProperty` method can throw three types of exceptions: `SecurityException`, `NullPointerException`, and `IllegalArgumentException`. - `SecurityException`: This exception is thrown if a security manager exists and its `checkPropertyAccess` method doesn't allow access to the specified system property. There is no explicit check or validation in the code snippet to prevent this exception. - `NullPointerException`: This exception is thrown if the `key` passed to `getProperty` is `null`. In the code snippet, all the keys passed to `getProperty` are string literals, which are not `null`, thus this exception is avoided. - `IllegalArgumentException`: This exception is thrown if the `key` passed to `getProperty` is an empty string. In the code snippet, none of the keys are empty strings, thus this exception is also avoided.
